turns.en: They are unbelievably cute. And sometimes my wife says to me, "Are you not curious?" Because they're both cute in very different ways. And my wife says, "Are you not curious to see what they would be like if we did have a third and a fourth? And they'd be cute in different ways."
turns.zh: 他们简直可爱到不行。我妻子有时会问我：“你不好奇吗？”因为两个孩子可爱的方式很不一样。她还会说：“你难道不好奇，如果咱们有了第三个、第四个孩子，他们会是什么样？而且他们也会可爱得很不一样。”

turns.en: You've done the iPod, the iPhone, Nest. All of them are kind of smash hit products. Do you ever sit there and think, what if I did a fourth act? What if I still do a fourth act and create the next Tony Fadell hit product?
turns.zh: 你做过 iPod、iPhone、Nest，都是爆款产品。你会不会坐在那儿想：如果我有第四幕呢？如果我现在还能来第四次，创造下一款 Tony Fadell 式爆款产品呢？

turns.en: Well, luckily, because of who I work with and the companies I invest in, I get to build and design a lot of products. I just don't have to do it day-to-day.
turns.zh: 嗯，幸运的是，因为和我合作的伙伴以及我投资的公司，我得以打造和设计很多产品。只是不需要每天都去做了。

turns.en: So, I worked with a company called Ledger, helping them design a set of products. I have a couple other products that I'm not talking about yet, but that I'm helping other companies with. So I get to design products and do this stuff without having to do the day-to-day anymore. And I think it's more rewarding because I get to work on—I have over a hundred direct investments now—and I'm able to work with all these teams doing AI in surgery, AI in textiles, AI in recycling, AI in drug discovery. So I get to work on all these different products. And I have even more fun than ever, and I'm able to reuse the things I've learned and the networks, and enable these other really smart teams who are dedicated and passionate to do that. So it's fun.
turns.zh: 所以，我和一家叫 Ledger 的公司合作，帮他们设计一系列产品。还有一些其他产品我暂时不能说，但也是在帮其他公司做。因此我可以做设计，而不用再天天做这些事。我觉得这反而更有成就感，因为我能实际参与——我现在有上百个直接投资项目——还能和所有这些团队合作，他们从事 AI 手术、AI 纺织品、AI 回收、AI 药物发现等。所以我可以在所有这些不同的产品上工作。而且我比以往玩得更开心，还能复用我学到的东西和人脉，让这些真正聪明、有热情和使命感的团队去做那些事。所以很有趣。

turns.en: Tony, thank you so much. An amazing place to end part one. We'll be back next week with part two. We're going to talk about life working with Steve Jobs, what you learned from him, and also lessons for careers more widely.
turns.zh: Tony，非常感谢。这是结束第一部分的绝佳时机。下周我们将带来第二部分。我们会聊到与 Steve Jobs 共事的经历、你从他身上学到了什么，以及更广泛的职业生涯启示。

consensus.en: Apple was near collapse before the iPod; bold risk-taking revived the company.
consensus.zh: 苹果在 iPod 之前濒临倒闭；大胆冒险让公司起死回生。

consensus.en: Successful products are painkillers, not vitamins; they must solve urgent user pain.
consensus.zh: 成功的产品是止痛药而非维生素；必须解决用户迫切痛点。

consensus.en: Habituation hides design flaws; staying beginner helps teams notice and fix them.
consensus.zh: 习惯化掩盖设计缺陷；保持初学者心态有助于发现并修复问题。

consensus.en: Existential threats force companies and people to make dramatic, necessary changes.
consensus.zh: 生存威胁迫使公司和个人做出剧烈而必要的改变。

consensus.en: Future AI hardware relies on a federation of devices, not one smartphone replacement.
consensus.zh: 未来 AI 硬件依赖设备联邦，而非单一手机替代品。

contrarian.en: Steve Jobs opposed Windows iPod for two generations, sacrificing sales to sell Macs.
contrarian.zh: 乔布斯两代之内反对 iPod 兼容 Windows，牺牲销量来推销 Mac。

contrarian.en: The iPod only took off after Jobs reversed course and allowed Windows compatibility.
contrarian.zh: iPod 直到乔布斯改弦更张、允许兼容 Windows 后才真正起飞。

contrarian.en: Apple's key iPod decision was outsourced to a journalist, not based on data.
contrarian.zh: 苹果对 iPod 的关键决策外包给记者，而非基于数据。

contrarian.en: The iPhone was born from fear of Nokia and Motorola killing the iPod, not pure vision.
contrarian.zh: iPhone 诞生源于对诺基亚和摩托罗拉扼杀 iPod 的恐惧，而非纯粹远见。

contrarian.en: General Magic failed because it solved pain before the pain existed; timing is everything.
contrarian.zh: General Magic 失败是因为在痛点出现前就解决问题；时机决定一切。

contrarian.en: People and companies rarely change until a near-death experience forces them to.
contrarian.zh: 人和公司极少主动改变，除非面临濒死体验的逼迫。
